subject: Invoice inquiry: metering lag, tax classification & payment hold
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novum-retail.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Question on Sep invoice — delayed usage window and VAT classification

Hi Kimberly,

We received the September invoice this morning and have put a temporary hold on payment while we understand two issues:

1) The invoice shows a large spike (~18% higher than our internal meter) for the period 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-03. Our engineering team says there was a delay in ingest -> attribution on Redwood's side that moved many requests into the next billing window. Can you confirm whether there was a processing lag or queue replay during that timeframe?

2) Your VAT line item labels the embed/usage as "standard VAT" which triggers our accounting to treat it differently. Historically similar usage from Redwood was zero-rated for our EU entity (we provided reverse charge elections). Please confirm the tax classification you used and, if needed, the evidence we should attach to our ERP to release payment.

I've attached the invoice we received and a CSV extract of our local usage for the disputed window. We need a short answer by EOD Thursday so our AP team can proceed.

Thanks,
Laura Chen\VP Finance — Novum Retail
Attachments:
- invoice_202609.pdf (pdf)
- sample_usage_window.csv (csv)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novum-retail.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Question on Sep invoice — delayed usage window and VAT classification

Hi Laura — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. We're looking into both items but wanted to confirm a few quick points while our billing and infra teams investigate:

- Did your internal CSV include both streaming and non-streaming generation calls? Our windows sometimes allocate streaming token counts differently when replays are applied.
- Can you share the HubSpot invoice ID (or the Redwood invoice number) you see in the PDF header? It helps us map to the billing execution log.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Ben (cc'd) will pull the ingress -> attribution timeline and any delayed replays for the 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-03 window.
- Marissa will confirm the VAT designation on the invoice and the tax evidence on file for Novum Retail (we have a reverse charge form from you dated 2025-11-02).

We treat any confirmed attribution lag caused by our reprocessing as eligible for provisional credit if it materially changed billed usage for a closed invoice period. We'll come back with initial findings by tomorrow afternoon.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize this.

Best,
Kimberly Park\Account Executive, Commercial\Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:27:00 +01:00
Subject: Fwd: Question on Sep invoice — delayed usage window and VAT classification

Kim / Marissa — quick engineering/billing readout below after initial log pull. Attaching the short sample (s3 link) with the ingested request timestamps.

Summary of findings (prelim):
- On 2026-09-02 between 02:10–03:05 UTC we observed a backlog on the ingest workers servicing eu-west-1 that caused queued requests to be processed in a later execution batch (same-day but crossed the midnight UTC boundary). Because our billing window uses business-day-aligned buckets for EU customers (local timezone cutover), roughly 42k tokens were attributed to the 2026-09-03 bucket instead of 2026-09-02.
- The net effect on the invoice is +370k tokens (~17.8% delta vs Novum's sample) for that closed window.
- Root cause: transient degradation in the reprocessor after a config roll that increased the queue retention TTL and caused a short replay. We've reverted the config and added a safety TTL cap.

Recommended remediation (billing):
- Offer a provisional credit for the 370k tokens on invoice INV-202609-887 (proportional to the token rate on that invoice).
- Mark this incident in the billing notes and tag the invoice with "metering-lag-adjustment" for downstream audit.

Marissa: can you confirm the VAT line treatment if we issue a credit? Historically issuing a credit preserves the original invoice VAT accounting (credit notes mirror tax treatment) but we should confirm Novum's preference for a corrected invoice vs credit note.

Attachments/links: https://s3.redwood-inference.com/for-customer/novum/usage-samples/202609-window.csv

-ben

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novum-retail.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 16:45:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Question on Sep invoice — delayed usage window and VAT classification

Hi Laura — following up with the resolution and next steps. Thanks for your patience.

What we did:
- Confirmed the ingest/replay backlog on 2026-09-02 (Ben's summary above).
- Issued a provisional credit equal to the token delta (370,000 tokens) on invoice INV-202609-887. The credit amount will appear as a line on your account and will reduce the balance due.
- We can either:
  • Issue a credit note that mirrors the original VAT treatment (reverse charge) — this keeps your ERP mapping unchanged; or
  • Reissue a corrected invoice with updated VAT lines if you prefer to show a single corrected invoice for audit.

Our recommendation: credit note (faster) unless your tax team needs a corrected document for a specific audit reason. Please confirm which you prefer and we will:
- Generate the credit note (or corrected invoice) by EOD Friday.
- Provide a one-page incident artifact with timestamps, the root-cause summary, and the S3 sample for your records (s3 link previously shared).

On the VAT question: we confirmed we have Novum Retail's reverse charge election on file (signed 2025-11-02). We will apply reverse charge treatment on the credit note so your AP can clear the hold without changing VAT liability. If your tax team requires a letter on Redwood letterhead confirming the classification and the credit action, we can add that to the artifact.

Please reply with "credit note" or "reissue invoice" and we will proceed.

Regards,
Marissa Cole\Billing Manager\Redwood Inference
